# Editor

## Editor requirement 1 — demonstrate the central result and report model fit

> **Original comment:** “Provide a compelling case that climate outweighs human effects … including a thorough analysis of the results, clearly indicating the variance explained by models.”

**Response.** We rebuilt the H1 presentation around time- and space-controlled analyses, added the corrected HVarPart extraction profiles, and report total adjusted $R^2$ separately from predictor allocation.

**Analytical result.** Climate exceeded human influence in `r format(spatial_climate_dominant_n, big.mark = ",")` of `r format(spatial_controlled_n, big.mark = ",")` controlled records (`r sprintf("%.1f", spatial_climate_dominant_pct)`%), while mean total adjusted $R^2$ across `r format(spatial_available_n, big.mark = ",")` available spatial SPD decompositions was `r sprintf("%.3f", spatial_mean_adjusted_r2)`.

**Changes in the revised article.** Results, “H1: Holocene human impact secondary to palaeoclimate” and “Result validation”; Fig. 3; Supplementary Figs. “HVarPart profiles, total fit, and fit–importance diagnostics” and “Signed counterparts”; Supplementary Tables “HVarPart model inventory” and “Analysis-level HVarPart profile comparison.”

> “These relative allocations partition the explained component of each fitted model and must not be interpreted as the fraction of total pollen variation explained; total adjusted $R^2$, signed contributions, zero-truncated compositions, and unique adjusted-$R^2$ fractions answer different questions.”

> “Palaeoclimate had greater relative importance than human SPD in `r format(spatial_climate_dominant_n, big.mark = ",")` of the `r format(spatial_controlled_n, big.mark = ",")` controlled records (`r sprintf("%.1f", spatial_climate_dominant_pct)`%; Fig. 3).”

## Editor requirement 2 — justify multiple scales and discuss limitations

> **Original comment:** “Justify the usage of data from multiple scales and fully discuss the limitations of your methods, particularly as raised by reviewer #2.”

**Response.** We now delimit the inference to continental and subcontinental pollen patterns, explain the mismatch among pollen-source areas, point climate values, 250/500 km SPD neighbourhoods, and regional events, and quantify the radius and proxy sensitivities on matched cohorts.

**Analytical result.** The radius comparison included `r format(radius_spatial_n, big.mark = ",")` spatial and `r radius_temporal_n` temporal matched comparisons; event inclusion included `r event_spatial_n` spatial and `r event_temporal_n` temporal matched observed-event comparisons.

**Changes in the revised article.** Methods, “Study interval, spatial units, and record cohorts,” “Human activity proxies,” and “Palaeoclimate predictors”; Discussion paragraphs on scale, SPD, climate modelling, events, and fixed climate zones; Supplementary Figs. “SPD-radius sensitivity” and “Human-event inclusion sensitivity.”

> “This inference is explicitly scale-bounded.”

> “The 250 km neighbourhood prioritises proximity, whereas the 500 km fallback increases radiocarbon coverage.”

## Editor requirement 3 — explain methods in detail

> **Original comment:** “Clearly explain your methods in detail.”

**Response.** We substantially expanded Methods to define record cohorts, pollen filtering and rarefaction, ten PAPs, posterior averaging, proxy construction, climate-model limitations, corrected HVarPart extraction, temporal and spatial controls, H1/H2 estimands, and reporting contracts.

**Analytical result.** The revised evidence package validates `r nrow(reporting_manifest)` registered artifacts with current hashes before rendering.

**Changes in the revised article.** The complete revised Methods and Supplementary Tables.

> “We retain these cohort labels throughout because they answer different questions and should not be conflated (Table 1).”

> “All reported result values are evaluated from registered CSV exports during rendering.”
